pagetitle: "About me"
---

Advancing the mobility transition towards sustainable mobility in all its definition (ecological, social, economical) motivates me to my PhD on the Wider Economic Benefits of Bicycle Infrastructure (WEBBI).

My research is highly relevant for adapting our cities to climate change and improving the urban life and the health of its citizens. I have experience in both academia and industry as well as in intercultural working environments. Additionally, I have high ambitions and a natural curiosity that brought me from a non-academic household to my current PhD position.

In the broader context, the Urban Transportation Lab at UTokyo and the Professorship of Mobility Policy at TUM strive to build a long-term fruitful collaboration with an already fixed research stay from Giancarlos Parady in Munich from October 2025 until January 2026. Thereafter, Parady's PhD student Uemura-san and I aim to amplify this relationship with mutual research stays in Munich and Tokyo, respectively.
